title: Sorting into categories
keyIdea: Put objects into the given groups, count how many are in each group, then order the groups from most to least.
familyTip: Give a mixed pile of toys with two labels (animals / vehicles). Sort, count each box, then say which has more.

visual.caption: Fair sorting idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: put each item in a given box
count how many in each box
order groups from most to least

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort into Animals/Vehicles, count each, order by count, catch mix-ups.

kid: Someone gives you the boxes. Put each thing in the right box.
Count how many are in each box. Say the number out loud.
Which box has more? Put the bigger group first when you order by count.
Sorting is not finished until you can say how many are in each category.
adult: K.MD.3: put objects into given groups, count each group, then order the groups by count. Words: group, count, most, least.
Common mistakes: ignoring the given labels; sorting but never counting; comparing without counts; mixing this up with free colour sorting.
In the lab your child sorts animals and vehicles, sets counts 4 and 3, orders most to least, and spots sorting without counting.

practice.hint: Use the given category name that fits a bus.
practice.explain: A bus is a vehicle, so it belongs in the Vehicles category.

practice.hint: K.MD.3 asks for counts in each category.
practice.explain: Classify first, then count the objects in each category.

practice.prompt: A box holds {n} toys. What is the count for that category?
practice.hint: The count equals how many objects sit in the box.
practice.explain: If the category has {n} objects, its count is {=n}.

practice.prompt: Category A has {a} and B has {b} (A is larger). How many more in A?
practice.hint: Subtract the smaller tally from the larger tally carefully.
practice.explain: When A has {a} and B has {b}, A has {=a-b} more.

practice.hint: Classify, then tally, then compare sizes.
practice.explain: Given categories first, then counts, then order by those counts.

pool.prompt: 4 animals and 3 vehicles. Animals count is…
pool.hint: Read the tally for the animals box only.
pool.explain: The animals category has 4 members, so its count is 4.

pool.hint: Compare 4 with 3, then list bigger first.
pool.explain: Animals (4) outnumber vehicles (3), so animals come first.

choices: Sort but never count the groups
pool.explain: Sorting without counting leaves out the required tallies.

pool.hint: Labels are given; counts come next.
pool.explain: Classify into given categories, then count and compare.

pool.prompt: Category A has {n} items. What tally do you write?
pool.hint: Write the number of items you counted.
pool.explain: The tally for that category is {=n}.

pool.prompt: Two categories have {a} and {b}. What is the total sorted?
pool.explain: All sorted objects total {=a+b} when groups are {a} and {b}.

pool.hint: Larger tally wins when ordering by count.
pool.explain: Blue’s count of 5 is greater than red’s 3.

pool.hint: Labels, then place, then compare counts.
pool.explain: Use given categories, classify all items, then compare tallies.
